page.layout: One page of text, single column, no margin notes. Running head at top centre. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: tus, colloquii, conversationis, vitæ denique omnis facilitatem decenti gravitate temperatam; qua sibi æquè superiorum, inferiorumque animos conciliat, ac devincit. Mitto alia multa Naturæ munera quæ in aliis diversis diversa in hunc unum collegit universa. Rarum Naturæ opus. Hæc etsi magna, & miranda, quæ ipsum magno illi Diguiereo totius Orbis miraculo tam intimum fecerunt, certè bonitas illa, & humanitas, & charitas incredibilis qua se suaque in omnes egentes effundit liberalissimè, præ cæteris virtutibus, certissimus est chara ëter[?] animi verè nobilis, certissi-maque verae nobilitatis insignia: dum quam potentiam, quam gratiam, quas opes multi ut leones in infirmioribus opprimendis; multi ut sues in libidinibus complendi perversè collocant, ille mitissimus, humanissimusque in hominum egentium levamine, atque juvamine, sedulò impendit. Ne sit aliud. Pauci sunt Nobiles in filiorum institutores tam largi: Pauci qui eos quorum ope non amplius egent, quos ut curent, nihil est, tamen in animi grati symbolum, donis tam magnis cumu-

page.notes: Catchword "lent" is the first word of the next page. Doubtful: "chara ëter" (the word after chara is printed with a mark over the e, possibly æter; marked [?]). The line-end hyphen in "certissi-maque" and "cumu-" is the printed hyphen, kept. Long s is normalised to plain s throughout, including "fues" (sues), "fe" (se) and "fymbolum" (symbolum). Printed "certiffi-" is read as certissi-, which assumes the ff is a long-s ligature.
